narrative.intro: Noridian Healthcare Solutions has $329M in federal contract obligations in FY2026 to date. The company received 7 awards so far, with an average award size of $47M, and obligations are up 39.2% year over year. Fiscal-year obligations show variability: FY21 totaled $324M, FY22 totaled $291M, FY23 totaled $154M, FY24 totaled $252M, FY25 totaled $236M, and FY26 totaled $329M. Market concentration is high: Direct Health and Medical Insurance Carriers accounts for $292M of obligations, while All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services accounts for $36.9M and Computer Systems Design Services accounts for $0. The FY2026 totals are partial and represent fiscal year to date activity, while award-value figures in some tables are total contract values rather than obligations. Use these figures to compare Noridian to peers, spot market concentration, and prioritize capture efforts where Direct Health and Medical Insurance Carriers dominates the company’s federal work.

sections.heading: How has Noridian Healthcare Solutions’ federal revenue trended over recent years?
sections.body: Noridian Healthcare Solutions’ obligations rose to $329M in FY26 after a low point of $154M in FY23. Noridian Healthcare Solutions recorded $324M in FY21, $291M in FY22, $252M in FY24, and $236M in FY25. The FY26-to-date total is up 39.2% year over year compared with the prior period.

sections.heading: Which markets account for the bulk of Noridian Healthcare Solutions’ federal work?
sections.body: Direct Health and Medical Insurance Carriers is the dominant market with $292M in obligations. All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services accounts for $36.9M, and Computer Systems Design Services accounts for $0. That concentration shows most federal dollars tied to health and insurance-related work.
